meta.note: Rule rows (PWC25 shape): id, world, statement (paraphrased), locators, speaker, mechanism, seam (AB code), derives (blocked slugs a playable model exists for), default_dial_reason, licence. Proposals: a batched reader (gpt-6-luna) read the books in shards of about 8,000 words; nothing here was human-checked, and no source text is kept.

rules.statement: A character’s maximum power-point reserve equals their POW. Spending power points fuels powers, and reaching 0 causes unconsciousness; rest restores the reserve to its maximum.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 4, Terms Used in Basic Roleplaying; Page 7, Step Five: Derived Characteristics (brp-orc#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a POW-sized reserve that returns with rest; a world can change its size or recovery rate, because power represents will or energy.

rules.statement: If the optional fatigue system is used, a character starts with STR+CON fatigue points and loses them through exertion; rest and other recovery restore them rapidly.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 8, Fatigue Points (Option) (brp-orc#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to STR+CON as the exertion reserve; a world can slow recovery or increase exertion losses, because strenuous activity tires the body.

rules.statement: If Sanity is used, its starting value is POW×5. At 0 Sanity the character is unplayable; losing too much at once can cause temporary or permanent insanity.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 8, Sanity (Option); Page 4, Terms Used in Basic Roleplaying (brp-orc#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a POW×5 mental-health track with play ending at zero; a world can change the threshold or consequences, because horrific experiences erode a character’s grasp on reality.

rules.statement: A fatal wound inflicts more hit-point damage than the character currently has; without medical or other intervention, death follows at the end of the next 12-second combat round.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 3, Terms Used in Basic Roleplaying (brp-orc#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to death after one combat round unless intervention occurs; a world can shorten or extend that window, because catastrophic injury overwhelms the body.

rules.statement: Power points are spent to use special abilities and can also be drained by other abilities. When the total reaches zero, the character falls unconscious.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 4, Terms Used in Basic Roleplaying (brp-orc#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to powers drawing from a shared reserve and unconsciousness at zero; a world can alter which effects drain it or what zero means, because the reserve represents usable will or energy.

rules.statement: A character dies if CON reaches 0. A character whose POW reaches 0 loses their soul and becomes catatonic.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 11, Constitution (CON); Page 11, Power (POW) (brp-orc#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to death at zero CON and soul-loss with catatonia at zero POW; a world can make either threshold recoverable or change its consequence, at the cost of weakening the link between body, will, and life.

rules.statement: In the optional hit-location system, head, abdomen, and each leg have one-third of total hit points, the chest has four-tenths, and each arm has one-quarter; fractions round up.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 7, Hit Points per Location (Option) (brp-orc#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to location-specific hit-point pools using the listed fractions; a world can adjust the proportions, because body regions differ in vulnerability.

rules.statement: When a characteristic changes because of injury, magic, or another cause, immediately recalculate every derived characteristic based on it. For example, reducing CON from 16 to 10 with SIZ 14 lowers maximum hit points from 15 to 12 and the major-wound level from 8 to 6.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Derived Characteristics, p. 13 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recalculating dependent values immediately; a setting can change which values depend on a characteristic, reflecting different rules for how bodies and abilities relate.

rules.statement: A character’s damage modifier comes from STR+SIZ and changes damage dealt by brawling and melee attacks; a result of zero or less inflicts no damage. For thrown weapons and bows, halve a positive modifier, rounding up, while firearms and other self-propelled weapons get none.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Damage Modifier, p. 13 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying the modifier only to the listed attack types; a world can broaden or narrow its use, reflecting how much physical strength contributes to weapon damage.

rules.statement: Maximum hit points are (CON+SIZ)/2, rounded up; at 2 or fewer hit points a character loses consciousness, and at 0 they die at the end of the following round. Lost hit points recover naturally at 1D3 per game week, with medical care able to speed recovery.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Hit Points, p. 14 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to this hit-point total and recovery rate; a world can use the optional CON+SIZ total for hardier characters, reflecting greater survivability.

rules.statement: With hit locations in use, humanoid location totals are based on fractions of maximum hit points: legs, abdomen, and head each get one-third; chest gets four-tenths; and each arm gets one-quarter, rounding up. Damage reduces both the struck location’s points and overall hit points; exceeding a location’s total disables it, and damage of twice that total crushes or severs it.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Hit Points by Hit Location, p. 14 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed location shares and injury thresholds; a world can omit locations or change the fractions, trading detail for simplicity or different bodily vulnerability.

rules.statement: Maximum power points usually equal POW. They recover at 1 per hour of sleep or total rest, or 1 per two hours of ordinary activity for POW 1–24; strenuous activity prevents recovery, and reaching 0 causes fainting until at least 1 is restored.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Power Points, p. 15 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to POW-based capacity and rest-based recovery; a world can use the provided faster recovery rates at higher POW or set another reserve, reflecting the setting’s model of spiritual energy.

rules.statement: Power points received from another source can raise a character’s own reserve to twice POW; further points are lost. While above the normal maximum, spending comes from the extra points first; extras neither regenerate normally nor renew, and disappear after a night’s sleep or another suitable point set by the gamemaster. Points stored in an item’s separate reserve do not count against this cap.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Power Points, p. 15 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary personal reserve cap of twice POW while allowing separate item reserves; a world can change the cap or duration, reflecting how unstable stored energy is.

rules.statement: With fatigue points in use, the maximum is STR+CON, and strenuous activity generally costs 1 per combat round; sprinting or backbreaking labor costs 1 per turn, and forced marches cost 1 per hour. Below 0, each negative point imposes a −1% penalty on skill, characteristic, and resistance rolls; reaching a negative total equal to the starting fatigue value incapacitates the character, while one point returns per minute without expenditure.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Fatigue Points, pp. 15–16 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to activity costs and penalties based on fatigue points; a world can use the simpler fatigue option instead, reflecting a preference for less resource tracking.

rules.statement: With simple fatigue, uninterrupted combat or difficult physical activity makes all skill rolls Difficult after CON×3 rounds. After CON×4 rounds, skills are treated as one-quarter their normal rating and physical action requires a successful Stamina roll; after CON×10 rounds, even basic actions require a Difficult Stamina roll, and the gamemaster may make skills Impossible or limit them to POW×1.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Simple Fatigue, p. 16 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to CON-based exhaustion thresholds; a world can use fatigue points or alter the thresholds, reflecting how much detail and endurance it wants physical exertion to have.

rules.statement: Base sanity points equal POW×5. Exposure to horror or mind-bending strangeness calls for a roll against current SAN, with a loss possible even on success; losing at least half the current SAN in five minutes causes temporary insanity. SAN does not recover naturally, may rise to 99 in specific circumstances, and some blasphemous knowledge can limit its maximum.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Sanity Points, p. 16 (brp-orc#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to POW-based SAN with loss from horrifying exposure and no natural recovery; a world can adjust recovery or knowledge-based limits, reflecting how lasting and corrosive its horrors are.

rules.statement: With the gamemaster’s permission, add one-fifth of a single related skill rating to the main skill rating for a roll. This bonus does not stack with other complementary skills, and a successful main roll grants an experience check only for that main skill.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Augments and Complementary skills, p. 34 (brp-orc#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing one relevant supporting skill for a modest rating bonus; a setting can narrow which skills qualify, because expertise outside the task’s context should not help.

rules.statement: A character may instead roll one supporting skill to adjust the main task’s difficulty by one step: success makes it easier, while failure makes it harder. This cannot be combined with the complementary-skill bonus; the supporting skill earns an experience check only if its roll succeeds and the main roll does not fail.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Augments and Complementary skills, p. 34 (brp-orc#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-step difficulty change from one successful augment; a world can make augmenting riskier or unavailable, since conflicting preparation can make the task harder.

rules.statement: A successful Command roll lets the leader add one-fifth of their Command rating as a skill bonus for subordinates each round they follow orders. The leader rolls each combat round, or each turn in mass combat; a fumble sparks insurrection and failure leaves the group confused or uninspired.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Command, p. 36 (brp-orc#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a round-by-round bonus only for followers who obey; a world can change the benefit or duration, with coordination and loyalty as the limiting costs.

rules.statement: Climbing generally uses one-fifth of normal movement, and a climber cannot take other actions while climbing. For an extended climb, call for a roll every minute or 10 meters; actions while clinging are difficult, and a fumble causes a fall.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Climb, p. 36 (brp-orc#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow movement and periodic checks during sustained climbing; a world can relax these limits for special surfaces or climbers, because exposure and loss of grip create danger.

rules.statement: A disguise can be detected by an onlooker who scrutinizes or speaks with the character, using an opposed Spot or Insight check; the disguised character may use Fast Talk in conversation to oppose detection. Suitable lighting, makeup, or facial changes may add up to 20% to the disguise roll at the gamemaster’s discretion.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Disguise, p. 37 (brp-orc#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to opposed scrutiny and a possible bonus of up to 20%; a world can make particular identities harder or easier to impersonate, because props, familiarity, and close inspection matter.

rules.statement: A successful Dodge changes a successful incoming attack into a failure; a special Dodge shifts the attack two result steps and a critical Dodge shifts it three, but no Dodge reduces an attack below failure. A character cannot Dodge and Parry in the same combat round, and each Dodge after the first in that round takes a cumulative −30% penalty.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Dodge, p. 37 (brp-orc#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one defense choice and increasingly penalized repeated Dodges; a world can alter how many attacks can be avoided, because repeated evasions strain a defender’s reactions.

rules.statement: Demolition skill is used to shape an explosion toward a specific result, such as bringing down a structure safely or breaching a door without damaging what is inside. At 60% skill or higher, ordinary uses succeed automatically; unstable explosives may require a check every round they are handled.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Demolition, p. 37 (brp-orc#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to automatic success for ordinary work at 60% and checks for unstable explosives; a world can raise the threshold or require more checks, because dangerous materials and difficult targets increase risk.

rules.statement: A successful First Aid attempt takes a full combat round and can treat one wound: it heals 1D3 hit points, revives an unconscious person, stops ongoing damage, or restores someone who reached 0 or fewer hit points in this or the prior round if healing raises them to at least 1. Special success heals 2D3, critical heals 3+1D3; failure prevents further First Aid on that wound, and each wound allows only one attempt.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: First Aid, pp. 39–40 (brp-orc#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing one round-long attempt per wound with limited healing; a world can make treatment easier with equipment or harder in hazardous conditions, reflecting access to care and risk of infection.

rules.statement: A successful Medicine treatment can choose a First Aid effect, double natural healing from 1D3 to 2D3 hit points per week, halt ongoing poison or disease damage, or stabilize the patient to recover 1D3–1 hit points or characteristic points per week. Special and critical successes improve wound healing to 2D3 and 1D3+3 hit points respectively, or characteristic recovery to 1D3 and 1D3+1; each use addresses one malady, and recovery from stabilization can be chosen only once per treatment week.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Medicine, p. 46 (brp-orc#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating one malady at a time and limiting stabilization recovery to once weekly; a world can accelerate treatment with advanced medical technology, at the cost of requiring suitable resources.

rules.statement: A grappler must establish a hold and then succeed at a Grapple roll each round to maintain it; the attacker may attempt one listed grapple effect per round starting the round after the hold is established. Taking another kind of action breaks the hold, and strangling removes the need for subsequent maintenance rolls but exposes the target to a CON×1% check each round or 1D3 damage.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Grapple and Grapple Effects, pp. 40–41 (brp-orc#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring repeated checks to keep a hold and limiting the attacker to one control effect per round; a world can make a choke more decisive, with the target risking recurring injury.

rules.statement: A successful Fast Talk briefly persuades someone to act against their better judgment, usually for only a few minutes; after that, a successful Idea roll may let the target reconsider. Persuade instead lasts until another Persuade attempt or a dramatic experience changes the target’s view.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Fast Talk, p. 39; Persuade, pp. 47–48 (brp-orc#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to brief, reversible influence for quick deception and longer-lived changes for deliberate persuasion; a world can make fast influence more durable, at the cost of stronger consequences when the target realizes what happened.

rules.statement: A successful Martial Arts result doubles the attack’s base damage roll when the same roll is within both the combat skill and Martial Arts rating, without doubling the damage modifier. For multiple attacks in a round, the Martial Arts rating must be divided among the attacks or assigned to just one.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Martial Arts, pp. 45–46 (brp-orc#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a doubled base-damage roll only when both skills succeed, while keeping the damage modifier unchanged; a world can permit broader use across attacks, diluting training across them.

rules.statement: A successful Psychotherapy treatment can restore 1D3–1 Sanity after a month, with special success restoring 1D3 and critical restoring 1D3+1; it can also diagnose an insanity or treat a diagnosed condition. Treatment takes four to five hours per month for each indefinite insanity and cannot raise Sanity above the applicable maximum.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Psychotherapy, p. 48 (brp-orc#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow, capped recovery through recurring treatment; a world can permit faster or broader therapy, but it requires substantial time and the underlying condition must be addressed.

rules.statement: To hide, a character needs adequate cover and is tested against an observer’s Spot; scant cover makes the attempt Difficult, no cover makes it impossible, and moving makes it Difficult. Moving more than a meter in a combat round requires both Hide and Stealth, while heat sensors or keen smell can still detect someone hidden from ordinary sight and sound.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Hide, p. 42 (brp-orc#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concealment from ordinary visual and aural detection only; a world can extend it to other senses, but specialized sensors and movement can defeat the concealment.

rules.statement: A successful Pilot roll reaches the intended destination, while most routine piloting is automatic and rolls are reserved for adverse or exceptional situations; outside combat, checks are made every four hours, and combat or vehicle maneuvers require one each round.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Pilot, p. 48 (brp-orc#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to automatic routine travel with checks at four-hour or round intervals when conditions demand them; a world can make routine operation more demanding, increasing the frequency of failure risks.

rules.statement: Casting a spell costs power points even on failure: normally each level costs 1 point, while a failed attempt loses 1 point and a fumble costs the full successful-cast amount. Reaching 0 power points makes the caster unconscious.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Costs of Magic [Page 56–57] (brp-orc#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging power points per spell level and incapacitating a caster at zero; a world can change the cost or zero-point consequence to make magic more or less dangerous, since exhaustion of magical reserves has bodily consequences.

rules.statement: A caster may cast only one spell per combat round, but can cast several levels of that spell together; each level costs 1 DEX rank and the maximum spell level is half the caster’s INT, rounded up. If the casting rank falls below zero, the spell resolves in the next round.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Casting Time / Spell Level [Page 57] (brp-orc#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one spell per round, with added levels costing both power points and time; a world can loosen the casting limit or raise the level cap for faster, stronger magic, at the cost of diminishing tactical constraints.

rules.statement: A spell affecting a living target must overcome either the target’s POW or power points in a resistance roll, as specified by the spell; determine power points before spending the spell’s cost. A willing recipient need not resist, but an unwilling recipient of a beneficial spell does, and an unconscious or debilitated target automatically fails.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Overcoming POW [Page 57] (brp-orc#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to resistance by the target’s stated defense, bypassed by consent; a world can make even beneficial effects resistible or allow different defenses to matter, reflecting its view of agency and magical force.

rules.statement: Two castings of the same spell never stack on one subject. When spells of unequal levels overlap, only the higher level works while it lasts; the lower level can resume afterward if its own duration remains, although all casting costs are paid.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Combining Spells [Page 57] (brp-orc#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to strongest-spell-only overlap and no same-spell stacking; a world can permit stacking or suppress lingering weaker effects to change how readily repeated magic compounds.

rules.statement: A magician can keep spells memorized up to half their INT, rounded up. Ready or dismiss each spell in 1 hour; spells beyond that capacity must be carried in a grimoire, and memorized spells remain available through sleep or unconsciousness until dismissed.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Memorization of Magic [Page 57] (brp-orc#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited memorized repertoire and an hour per change; a world can expand capacity or shorten preparation time, trading constraints on flexibility for easier access to magic.

rules.statement: Binding a familiar requires a suitable creature, three months of close ritual preparation with no separation longer than a day, a permanent 1 POW sacrifice, and success in a POW-versus-POW contest. Failure loses the POW and bars that creature from becoming a familiar; success expends all current power points and creates an unbreakable link.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: The Magician’s Familiar [Page 58] (brp-orc#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one active familiar and a costly, extended binding; a world can reduce the time or sacrifice, or permit multiple bonds, with the cost representing the depth and exclusivity of the magical tie.

rules.statement: While a familiar is within the magician’s POW in meters, the magician can spend its power or fatigue points instead of their own, perceive through its senses for 1 power point per full turn, issue a telepathic command for 1 point, and speak through it for 1 point per sentence. The creature loses consciousness at 0 power points or at fatigue equal to twice its normal total below zero.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: The Magician’s Familiar [Pages 58–59] (brp-orc#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to shared resources and remote sensory or command abilities only within the bond’s range; a world can widen the range or remove per-use costs, at the risk of making the companion a nearly consequence-free extension.

rules.statement: A wizard’s staff takes six months to construct, requires constant oversight and a permanent 1 POW sacrifice, and can hold up to the maker’s POW at construction minus that sacrificed point. It regenerates power points at its owner’s rate, but cannot transfer them to the owner and dies permanently if reduced to 0.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: The Wizard’s Staff [Pages 59–60] (brp-orc#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a durable but finite power reserve that cannot refill its owner and is destroyed at zero; a world can change capacity or allow transfer, with the sacrifice and construction effort explaining the staff’s limits.

rules.statement: A fumbled spell loses all power points committed to it and prevents another use for one combat round; if it deals damage, a failed Luck roll redirects it to an unintended target. A failed spell costs 1 power point and has no useful effect, while success spends the required cost and works.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Magic Spell Success Levels, p. 61 (brp-orc#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these failure costs; a world can make mishaps harsher or gentler, reflecting how dangerous unstable magic is.

rules.statement: A special spell success can add a fitting special damage quality, increase an aspect such as range or influence to 150%, or raise a resistance level by 1.5 times. A critical success ignores armor and deals maximum damage, or doubles a suitable non-damage effect or resistance level.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Magic Spell Success Levels, p. 61 (brp-orc#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to enhanced effects at special and critical success; a world can narrow or broaden the bonus, reflecting how precisely magic responds to exceptional casting.

rules.statement: Unless a spell says otherwise, its maximum range is 100 meters, and a directly affected target must be in line of sight. Spells ordinarily take effect in the casting round and last for the duration specified, commonly one round, 10 rounds, or 15 minutes.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Magic Spells, p. 61 (brp-orc#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these range and duration conventions; a world can change them to make magic more local or persistent, reflecting its reach and stability.

rules.statement: Change transforms 3 SIZ per level for 15 minutes and costs 1 power point per level; a resisting target requires overcoming its POW. The new form has its shape’s outward traits and natural abilities, but retains its characteristics, skills, wounds, and other existing conditions.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Change, p. 62 (brp-orc#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to form-specific outward traits with retained statistics and injuries; a world can allow deeper transformation, at the cost of changing more than appearance and natural capabilities.

rules.statement: Control costs 3 power points per level, lasts 10 rounds, and each level can affect one intelligent target if the caster wins a POW-versus-POW resistance roll. The caster must concentrate; distraction or fighting makes controlled targets collapse, while objectionable orders allow an Idea-based attempt to balk or break free.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Control, p. 63 (brp-orc#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concentration and resistance as limits; a world can make control easier or harder to maintain, reflecting the strain and moral resistance involved.

rules.statement: Countermagic costs 1 power point per level and lasts 5 minutes; incoming spells must overcome its level or rebound on their caster, and spells that fail to penetrate two such shields dissipate. Its protection interacts with Protection and is ineffective against Fire and Frost.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Countermagic, p. 63 (brp-orc#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spell-level resistance and the listed exceptions; a world can broaden or restrict what magic wards stop, reflecting the limits of its defensive tradition.

rules.statement: Teleport moves 3 SIZ per level instantly, costs 1 power point per level, and normally reaches 1,000 meters; extra levels add 1,000 meters each. A resisting living target or an affixed object requires an overcoming roll, while deliberately placing a target inside solid matter costs 3 power points per level and a 0/1D3 Sanity roll.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Teleport, p. 68 (brp-orc#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to whole-object transport, resistance for unwilling or attached targets, and an added price for solid-matter placement; a world can change range or danger to reflect the risks of transit.

rules.statement: Ward permanently protects a square of up to 9 square meters marked by four objects prepared in a preliminary ritual. Its boundary counters passing power at Countermagic 1 and blasts objects crossing it at Blast 1; additional levels enlarge a dimension by 3 meters or add one level to both effects, and moving or destroying the markers ends the ward.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Ward, pp. 69–70 (brp-orc#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a marker-bounded ward that remains until disrupted or dispelled; a world can alter its size and defensive strength, with the cost of additional casting levels.

rules.statement: A disease-carrying mutant is immune to its own disease, which has POT 2D10 and spreads by touch or another specified route within CON range; exposed creatures resist with CON against its POT. The major version has POT 4D10 or carries two diseases with separate routes.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Disease Carrier, p. 73 (brp-orc#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one disease at 2D10 POT; a world can increase potency or add a second vector, at the cost of a more dangerous infection risk.

rules.statement: A group-intelligent mutant shares experience with its linked colony. The minor link reaches CON meters and conveys vague sensations or behavioral urges; the major link permits full telepathic communication at unlimited distance.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Group Intelligence, p. 73 (brp-orc#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to short-range impressions; a world can allow unlimited full communication, making the colony’s shared awareness far more capable.

rules.statement: Minor Hardy halves rolled damage from one chosen injury type, rounding down. Major Hardy adds this resistance and allows action at 0 or negative hit points until reaching negative hit points equal to CON; without healing to at least 1 hit point within five minutes, the mutant dies.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Hardy, p. 73 (brp-orc#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to halved damage from one selected source; a world can also permit action past zero health, with death threatened unless healing arrives within five minutes.

rules.statement: Keen Sense grants +20% to relevant skills when minor and +40% when major; hearing and vision range double or quadruple, respectively. The heightened sense is also harmful: intense stimulation requires an Idea roll to avoid a round of stun, and the roll is Difficult for the major version.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Keen Sense, p. 74 (brp-orc#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a skill bonus and a heightened range; a world can make intense sensory exposure more dangerous, risking a lost round.

rules.statement: Psychic abilities generally spend power points even on failure: failure costs 1, a fumble costs the full intended amount, and success costs the stated amount. A psychic at 0 power points is unconscious and cannot use abilities; a cost below 1 per combat round is charged only after the roll is resolved.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Cost of Psychic Abilities, p. 76 (brp-orc#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to power-point expenditure with a reduced failure charge; a world can make failed attempts costly, with exhaustion as the limiting consequence.

rules.statement: An ability used against an unwilling opponent generally requires a resistance roll, often POW against POW or current power points against current power points; willing targets need no resistance roll. Instant abilities resolve in the powers phase by INT rank, while longer abilities are announced and rolled on DEX rank, then take effect in the next round’s powers phase.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Using Psychic Abilities, p. 77 (brp-orc#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to opposed resistance for unwilling targets and automatic effect on willing targets; a world can make psychic influence slower by requiring a later-round resolution.

rules.statement: During astral psychic combat, combatants must be within the higher of their POW-in-meters ranges and attack with current power-point resistance rolls. If both succeed each loses 1D3 power points; if only one succeeds the other loses 1D3, and if neither succeeds there is no result; reaching 0 power points returns a combatant to their body unconscious.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Psychic Combat, p. 78 (brp-orc#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to power-point attrition that ejects an incapacitated astral combatant; a world can make the fight lethal by allowing a winner to continue against the unconscious opponent.

rules.statement: Training a new psychic ability takes weeks equal to POW minus 30 and requires sacrificing 1 permanent POW plus a successful Luck roll; failure allows another attempt after further training and sacrifice. An involuntary awakening instead costs 2 permanent POW and grants the new ability at POW×5.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Gaining New Psychic Abilities, p. 77 (brp-orc#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to learning through training with a permanent POW sacrifice; a world can permit sudden stress-triggered awakening, at a larger POW cost.

rules.statement: Mind Control requires a successful power use and a successful POW-versus-POW resistance contest; its cost is 1 power point per 3 points of target POW, rounded up, plus 1 per further combat round. The psychic controls the target’s movement and speech but must concentrate for actions beyond sleeping; the target can resist once per round and can attempt a new escape contest each round.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Mind Control, p. 84 (brp-orc#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to control of movement and speech with recurring power-point upkeep; a world can raise the escape difficulty or cost, justified by stronger mental defenses.

rules.statement: Mind Shield costs at least 1 power point and lasts one full turn per point spent. Each point resists psychic attacks, can protect against 1 sanity loss per horrific encounter while active, and temporarily adds 3 POW for resistance against non-psychic influences; it must already be active to foil passive psychic detection.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Mind Shield, p. 84 (brp-orc#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-turn-per-point protection; a setting can narrow which threats it blocks, explained by differing psychic disciplines.

rules.statement: Active Precognition costs 1 power point to activate plus points based on the requested time step: 1 reaches one combat round, 5 one day, 8 one year, and 10 one hundred years. Passive use has no power-point cost and is rolled secretly by the gamemaster; results range from misleading or unclear visions to detailed guidance on a special or critical success.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Precognition, pp. 84–85 (brp-orc#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to costly active glimpses and free prompted passive visions; a world can increase the price or add fatigue or sanity costs because longer-range futures are harder to perceive.

rules.statement: Psychometry senses impressions absorbed by an inanimate object or place, costing power points equal to its SIZ, minimum 1, plus points for the time step of its last use. A failed attempt cannot be repeated on that specific item or place until the skill improves; passive gamemaster-triggered use costs nothing.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Psychometry, p. 85 (brp-orc#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one use-history impression at a SIZ- and age-based cost; a world can restrict what impressions survive because objects retain only strong traces.

rules.statement: Telekinesis costs 1 power point per 3 SIZ per combat round and moves an object at normal movement within POW-meter range; extra points extend throwing range by 15 meters each or increase speed. Holding it requires continued power expenditure, and unconsciousness or a major wound drops it.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Telekinesis, p. 86 (brp-orc#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weight-scaled, round-by-round upkeep; a world can allow longer holds or heavier loads at increased cost, reflecting the strain of sustained force.

rules.statement: Telepathy requires a successful power use and, for an unwilling target, a successful POW resistance contest; reading costs 1 point per 3 target POW, rounded up, and lasts through the current combat round. A link can convey thoughts or memories, read surface thoughts, implant a false memory or sensation, or search buried memories; each further round costs 1 point, and targets can try to break the link each round.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Telepathy, pp. 86–87 (brp-orc#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to brief, resisted mental access with per-round upkeep; a world can make implanted impressions last longer or be harder to detect, at the cost of stronger defenses or greater power.

rules.statement: A sorcerer must have POW 16 or higher. Known spells must be readied in memory to cast, the mind holds spell levels up to INT, readying takes one combat round per spell point, casting usually takes one round and costs the spell’s points, and its duration is normally POW combat rounds; a cast spell cannot be recalled, though its effect can usually be ended early or extended by casting it again.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Sorcery, pp. 87–90 (brp-orc#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an INT-limited ready-spell capacity and POW-based duration; a world can enlarge capacity or alter duration, justified by unusual training or magical traditions.

rules.statement: A spell affects one person, entity, area, or thing; separate targets require separate castings. Only one spell can affect an object at a time, and adding another has no effect but still consumes its power points; compatible spells may coexist on a person at the gamemaster’s discretion.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Spells per Object and Spells per Person, p. 93 (brp-orc#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one spell per object and discretionary stacking on people; a world can permit more effects on objects, justified by rare enchantment capacity.

rules.statement: An effect that boosts a characteristic by its maximum listed amount can become permanent on a D100 roll of 00. The recipient then cannot benefit from that spell again and must permanently lose 9 points from other characteristics; where allegiance is used, the change also grants 1D8 allegiance to a force associated with change or randomness.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Pages 97–102, characteristic-boosting spells (brp-orc#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary boosts; a world can make a maximum boost permanent on 00, with a permanent 9-point characteristic loss and possible allegiance as the price.

rules.statement: A demon summoned with Summon Demon costs 9 power points to appear. Binding it requires a resistance roll of the summoner’s POW against the demon’s POW and permanently costs 1 POW, or 3 POW to bind it permanently into an object; the sorcerer’s INT limits the total demon POW they can keep bound.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Pages 99–100, Summon Demon (brp-orc#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a demon that obeys only its binder; a world can allow permanent object bindings, paid for with more POW and constrained by INT.

rules.statement: An ordinary demon binding ends if the binder dismisses the demon, the demon or binder dies, or the demon’s true name is learned and used in a successful rebinding. A permanent binding ends only if its containing object or place is destroyed.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 100, Summon Demon (brp-orc#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed release and destruction conditions; a world can make permanent bindings harder to break, at the cost of making their vessels critical.

rules.statement: Summon Elemental brings an elemental after 1D6 combat rounds, once the sorcerer has spent 1D8 rounds specifying it and knows the spell linked to that element. The elemental arrives ready to perform one task.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 100, Summon Elemental (brp-orc#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one task per summoned elemental; a world can change its arrival delay or permit binding, risking elemental hostility.

rules.statement: Undo Sorcery removes one level of an affected spell or enchanted item per level cast; if insufficient, it reduces the effect’s level but does not end it. Refutation can contest Undo Sorcery, and the losing spell’s power points are spent without effect.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Pages 98–99, Refutation and Undo Sorcery (brp-orc#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-for-one level removal; a world can let defensive Refutation contest dispelling, with the loser wasting its power points.

rules.statement: Superpowers have levels bought with character-point budget; levels usually increase damage, range, or another listed attribute, and damage-dealing powers generally inflict 1D6 per level. Character failings can add budget, but are capped at half the starting budget rounded up; power modifiers cannot return more than half a power’s initial cost rounded down.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Pages 103–105, How Superpowers Work; Character Failings and Power Modifiers (brp-orc#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to level-based powers bought from a limited budget; a world can raise the budget through failings or limitations, accepting real play disadvantages.

rules.statement: A special weakness can harm a character within 15 meters, with the failing’s budget reward set by its damage or characteristic loss and the substance’s rarity. The character cannot buy a power that resists that chosen weakness.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 104, Benefits From Character Failings Table (brp-orc#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed weakness damage and range; a world can make weaknesses more severe or common for more points, while forbidding resistance to the chosen weakness.

rules.statement: A power modifier can limit a power’s uses, targets, range, cost, or operating conditions in return for budget points. Its reward applies to one power, and no power can gain more than half its initial cost, rounded down, from modifiers.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Pages 104–105, Power Modifiers (brp-orc#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to individual, capped power limitations; a world can broaden the available modifiers, but each must impose a meaningful restriction.

rules.statement: When a superpower is permanently removed, return its spent points to the character budget and remove any failings or modifiers that depended on it; the points may be spent later depending on why and how the power was lost. Removing a failing or modifier also requires GM permission and may require replacing its budget value with an equal failing or modifier, or deducting it from surplus or future rewards.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Losing Superpowers; Losing Character Failings or Power Modifiers (brp-orc#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to returning power points and requiring equivalent replacement for shed limitations; the GM can loosen this for campaign reasons, while preserving the character-budget balance.

rules.statement: Projection requires line of sight and uses DEX×2 as its base chance; damage modifier never adds to projected powers. On failure, the shot goes wide in a direction determined by 1D4, and a Luck roll determines whether it causes collateral damage; on a fumble, power points are lost and the user cannot use that power for one combat round after the fumble round.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: The Projection Skill (option) (brp-orc#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a clear line of sight and applying the stated miss and fumble risks; a setting can change those limits to suit its targeting technology or power style.

rules.statement: For superpowers, failure spends the power points but produces no harmful complication, while success produces the stated effect. A fumble also loses the points and blocks that power for one further combat round; a special success increases effectiveness, and a critical doubles an appropriate non-damaging effect or ignores armor for damaging effects.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Powers and Success Levels (brp-orc#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spending power points on failed uses and scaling effects on special or critical results; a world can simplify outcome adjustments, trading nuance for speed.

rules.statement: When Resistance, Protection, Armor, and Absorption all apply to an attack, resolve them in that order: Resistance may stop it, Protection lowers its power level, Armor reduces damage, and Absorption converts remaining damage into power points.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Absorption, Armor, Protection, and Resistance (brp-orc#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to this fixed defensive sequence; a setting may alter the order, but doing so changes which defense can intercept or convert the attack.

rules.statement: Absorption works continuously against one chosen damaging energy type, absorbing 1 damage point per level and storing it as power points. If the character or battery has no room for the stored points, excess damage affects the character; energy cannot be moved between a battery and the character’s reserve unless the battery also has Absorption.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Absorption (brp-orc#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to type-specific absorption limited by available storage; a world can allow broader absorption or easier reserve transfers, at the cost of making energy storage less restrictive.

rules.statement: Adaptation provides survival in one chosen hostile environment per level; activating it costs 1 power point per SIZ, followed by 1 power point per full turn, and its duration is 1 full turn. It protects against environmental conditions, not attacks that use those conditions, and some environments require multiple adaptations.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Adaptation (brp-orc#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one environment per level and ongoing power-point upkeep; the GM can let related environments share protection, balancing versatility against the cost of broader coverage.

rules.statement: An Alternate Form costs no power points to use and switches bodies within a combat round; if the alternate body becomes unconscious, the character returns to the original. On switching back, each resource is set to the lower of its values in the two forms, and debilitating conditions persist across forms.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Alternate Form (brp-orc#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to carrying the worse resource total and any debilitating condition across forms; a world can make forms more independent, at the cost of easing the consequences of transformation.

rules.statement: Barrier creates a grounded wall within 15 meters that lasts 15 minutes and costs 3 power points per level; each level makes 1 cubic meter of material, and each meter of thickness has 30 hit points. When the power ends, the barrier disappears unless it consists of material that would normally remain.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Barrier (brp-orc#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a grounded, temporary barrier with durability tied to its thickness; a world can permit unsupported or lasting barriers, increasing the power’s ability to change the environment.

rules.statement: Energy points can come from the character’s body or an external battery; the gamemaster may permit either source to fuel a power. A battery can be targeted, and several supplies may be assigned to different powers or shared among them.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Power points (before Extra Hit Points) (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to assigning internal energy to personal powers and batteries to external gear; a world can allow sources to cross-fuel, at the risk that an external supply can be targeted.

rules.statement: A power may cost nothing to activate, charge once per activation, or require payment each round it remains active. Spent personal points return according to the power-point rules, while batteries must be recharged; matching-energy Absorption can replenish either.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Power points (before Extra Hit Points) (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed activation or maintenance cost; a world can make battery recharge the key constraint, since external reserves must be replenished.

rules.statement: A Force Field supplies 10 armor per level against a specified attack or energy type, costs 1 power point per round and 1 per damage absorbed, and can cover a target within 15 meters. If one blow exceeds its specified protection or the user’s available points, the field dissipates.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Force Field, p. 117 (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to protecting one SIZ of target per level against a chosen type; a world can allow broader or multiple-type coverage, with separate purchases and escalating energy costs.

rules.statement: Protection reduces the level of an incoming superpower of its chosen energy type by its own level, potentially reducing it to zero. It costs 1 power point per level each combat round; protection against different types must be purchased separately.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Protection, p. 118 (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reducing only matching attack types; a world can broaden protection to additional types, but each type requires its own purchase.

rules.statement: When active, Size Change alters SIZ by one point per level in the purchased direction and costs 1 point per level to activate, with no maintenance cost. Unconsciousness, sleep, depleted points, cancellation, or failure to hold the form after a major wound ends the change and restores normal size.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Size Change, p. 120 (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-way growth or shrinkage per purchase; a world can permit both directions only by requiring separate purchases, and interruption risks losing the changed form.

rules.statement: Stretching extends the body 1 meter per level; each meter extended reduces current STR by 1. At twice CON in levels, it permits exceptional squeezing and reshaping; imitating another power requires an Idea roll and double that power’s point cost, granting half the Stretching level temporarily.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Stretching, p. 121 (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited extension with a strength penalty; a world can allow temporary imitation of other powers, paid for at double cost and limited to half the Stretching level.

rules.statement: Teleport moves 1 SIZ per level instantly within 1,000 meters for 1 power point per level. Moving an unwilling target requires overcoming their power points; a failed fumble-related Luck check can cause 3D6 damage, while deliberate attacks using teleport have additional costs and avoidance rolls.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Teleport, p. 124 (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to voluntary transport within range; a world can allow offensive placement into solid matter, but it costs extra and gives the target a chance to avoid it.

rules.statement: Transfer moves hit points, power points, fatigue points, or sanity points by touch at 1 point per level each round, never more than the giver has. Recipients cannot exceed their normal maximum except for power points, and unwilling targets may resist using the characteristic appropriate to the resource.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Transfer, pp. 124–125 (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a touch-based exchange capped by level and available resources; a world can allow transfers to unwilling targets, but resistance and the giver’s own resource loss limit the effect.

rules.statement: Weather Control alters local conditions within 15 meters per level, changing temperature by 5°C per level or moving conditions one step per round; it costs 3 points per level to activate and 1 per round to maintain. When it ends, conditions drift back one step per round, and it cannot directly inflict damage.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Weather Control, pp. 125–126 (brp-orc#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to non-damaging weather changes that gradually fade; a world can permit stronger atmospheric effects, but direct harm remains outside this power.

rules.statement: Percentile rolls have five outcome grades: fumbles, failures, ordinary successes, special successes at 1/5 or less of the skill rating, and critical successes at 1/20 or less. A 00 is always a fumble; a fumble has harmful or obstructive consequences, while critical results provide the best outcome.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Evaluating Success or Failure, p. 128 (brp-orc#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the five grades as the default; a world can soften fumbles or change the thresholds, trading swingy, dangerous outcomes for steadier resolution.

rules.statement: A resistance test uses 50% + (active factor × 5) − (passive factor × 5), with each point of difference changing the chance by 5%. A difference of 10 or more normally makes the result automatic, though the GM may permit a 01 or 00 exception; power-point contests can determine whether a power affecting or controlling a target takes effect.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Resistance Rolls, p. 129 (brp-orc#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the resistance formula and automatic outcomes at a 10-point gap; turn on exceptional rolls when dramatic reversals are desired, at the cost of certainty.

rules.statement: For cooperative skill use, designate one lead and have helpers roll. A helper’s critical, special, or ordinary success raises the lead’s skill by 50%, 30%, or 20%, respectively; if all helpers fail, reduce it by 10%, and any helper fumble reduces it by 50%.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Cooperative Skill Rolls, p. 130 (brp-orc#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use one lead and these listed modifiers by default; a world can limit assistance to reflect practical constraints, making teamwork less powerful.

rules.statement: In the default opposed-skill method, the higher degree of success wins, but each degree of success achieved by a successful loser reduces the winner’s result by one degree. Equal degrees are decided by the higher die roll.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Opposed Skill Rolls, p. 130–131 (brp-orc#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use degrees of success and downgrade the winner by the loser’s successful degrees; a world can choose one of the simpler alternate contests for faster resolution.

rules.statement: Difficulty changes a skill rating before a roll: Easy doubles it, Average leaves it unchanged, and Difficult halves it, rounding up. Automatic tasks require no roll, while Impossible tasks fail outright, though the GM may allow a 1% chance in a suitably plausible case.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Difficulty Modifiers, p. 132 (brp-orc#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed difficulty steps, with Automatic and Impossible at the extremes; a world can permit rare Impossible-task successes to favor extraordinary luck over strict limits.

rules.statement: A character may spend 5 power points after a percentile roll to reroll it, with the second result final, or spend 5 to replace a skill test with a Difficult Luck roll. Spending 3 power points ignores 1 damage from one attack; reaching 0 power points causes exhaustion and fainting until at least 1 point returns.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Fate Points, p. 133 (brp-orc#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow these listed expenditures by default; a world can restrict or remove them to preserve uncertainty, since using them depletes the reserve and can cause fainting.

rules.statement: Optional fate-point uses let a player spend 6 power points per result grade to improve their own roll, or spend power points equal to a weapon’s full damage range to deal that maximum damage on a successful strike. A variable GM-set cost can also establish a useful detail, resource, or contact; these uses do not earn experience checks.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Fate Points, p. 134 (brp-orc#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Keep these as optional high-adventure permissions; a world can exclude them, especially where preserving helplessness matters, while allowing them makes power points buy narrative control.

rules.statement: A game turn lasts 5 minutes, a combat round lasts 12 seconds, and one turn contains 25 combat rounds. A character normally moves 10 movement units per combat round; the GM can temporarily reduce this for burdens, fatigue, caution, terrain, or weather.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Turn and Combat Round, pp. 134–136 (brp-orc#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated durations and baseline movement; a world can adjust the unit’s distance or movement penalties to suit its scale and conditions.

rules.statement: After a qualifying experience check, roll percentile dice and add half INT, rounded up; improvement succeeds only if the result exceeds the current skill rating. A success adds 1D6 skill points, or the player may choose +3 before rolling; epic and superhuman campaigns may use 1D8 or 1D10 instead, with fixed alternatives of +4 or +5.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Making an Experience Roll / Increasing Skills by Experience, p. 139 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gradual skill growth after successful experience; a world can raise the increase die for faster advancement, making characters improve more rapidly.

rules.statement: Training with a more skilled teacher takes hours equal to the learner’s current skill rating. A successful Teach roll adds 1D6, failure adds nothing, and a fumble subtracts 1D3; training cannot raise a skill above 75% by default.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Skill Training, p. 139 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to costly, teacher-led improvement capped at 75%; a setting can permit higher training, at the cost of time, compensation, and the risk of a fumbled lesson.

rules.statement: Research takes as long as training but need not incur the same expense. Afterward, a successful experience roll adds 1D6–2 to the skill, or the character may choose +2; research can exceed 75%.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Researching, p. 139 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slower, self-directed learning that can surpass the training cap; a world can vary its research costs or require practical experience, reflecting access to resources.

rules.statement: A successful POW resistance match against an opponent with equal or greater POW can earn a POW improvement check when the chance of success is 50% or less. The check succeeds on D100 at or below five times the gap between the character’s current POW and the species’ usual maximum-plus-minimum total; a success adds 1D3–1 POW, or the player may choose +1 before rolling.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: POW Increases, p. 140 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to small, uncertain POW growth earned through difficult contests; a world can change the allowed characteristics or maximums, with advancement tied to testing oneself.

rules.statement: Characteristic training takes 25 hours per current characteristic point and then adds 1D3–1. STR and CON are capped by the highest original STR, CON, or SIZ; DEX and CHA are capped at one-and-a-half times their original value, rounded up.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Characteristic Increase through Training, p. 140 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to demanding training with growth limits based on the character’s starting body and traits; a world can change the regimen or caps, trading plausibility for greater advancement.

rules.statement: As an optional aging rule, starting at age 41 and each year afterward, roll 2D6 to determine characteristic-loss checks: results from 6–8 cause none, while other results cause 1–4 checks as listed. Each check rolls on the characteristic table; a characteristic reaching 0 causes death, while POW and EDU do not decline.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Aging and Inaction (Option), pp. 140–141 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gradual physical and social-trait decline from age 41; a world can disregard or alter it for longevity, self-care, or nonhuman lifespans.

rules.statement: Combat rounds last 12 seconds. A character can activate one power per round; most powers take a full round to prepare and take effect at the beginning of the next round, and their power-point cost is paid at the INT rank when used.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Powers, p. 143 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one power action per round with a delayed effect for most powers; a world can make powers faster through exceptions, while power points remain the expenditure.

rules.statement: A character can move up to 30 meters in a round if doing nothing but defending. Moving 6–15 meters halves their DEX rank, while 16–29 meters reduces it to one-quarter; an attack can be combined with movement of up to 5 meters.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Move / Attack, p. 144 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to distance reducing action speed; a world can adjust movement and rank penalties to suit its pace, with greater travel limiting when the character acts.

rules.statement: Each parry or dodge after the first in a round takes a cumulative –30% skill penalty, and a chance below 1% cannot be attempted. A fully defensive stance allows parries and dodges together; fighting defensively instead trades attacks for one extra dodge that avoids the successive-action penalty.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Parry / Dodge / Fight Defensively, pp. 144–145 (brp-orc#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to increasingly difficult repeated defense; a world can change the penalty or defensive options, balancing protection against the ability to attack.

rules.statement: A special entangle made from at least 3 meters away (except a garrote at close range) stops the target moving until the end of the current round and through the next. On the following round the target can try Agility to escape, STR versus the attacker’s STR to wrench the weapon free, or cut it if able; a successful Dodge or Wrestle also negates it, but only on that next round.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Entangling (brp-orc#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-round restraint with next-round escape attempts; a world can adjust duration or escape options to reflect weapon design and how securely it binds.

rules.statement: A special success with a pointed or thrusting weapon doubles that weapon’s rolled damage dice and modifier, but does not double the attacker’s separate damage modifier. The weapon remains lodged until removed; significant movement causes another roll for half the weapon’s damage, without damage modifier or armor protection.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Impaling (brp-orc#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a lodged weapon and movement-triggered wound damage; a world can reduce these consequences for cinematic combat, at the cost of less consequential injuries.

rules.statement: A special unarmed throw or shield hit can knock a target back: compare rolled damage before armor against the target’s SIZ. If the target loses, push them 1 meter per 5 damage; striking an obstacle deals 1D6 damage per 3 meters or part thereof, and the target must pass Agility or fall prone.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Knockback (brp-orc#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to damage-versus-SIZ resistance and distance-scaled collision harm; a world can change the displacement or collision severity to suit its desired combat physics.

rules.statement: A character who gives up every attack for the round gets one extra Dodge attempt without the usual cumulative –30% penalty, and subsequent Dodge or parry attempts do not worsen an existing penalty. This cannot be combined with attacks or other offensive actions, and Dodge and parry cannot both occur at the same DEX rank.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Fighting Defensively (brp-orc#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trading offense for a penalty-free defensive attempt; a world can make defense more or less generous, with the cost expressed as foregoing all offensive action.

rules.statement: A character with a combat skill of at least 100% may split it into attacks each rated at least 50%, allocating all skill points without rounding fractions upward. The first attack uses the normal DEX rank and each later attack occurs 5 DEX ranks later; an attack at rank 0 or below cannot be made.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Attacks and Parries Over 100% (Option) (brp-orc#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to splitting excess skill into multiple later attacks; a world can disallow or expand this option to control how strongly exceptional skill increases attack frequency.

rules.statement: When a character suffers a fatal wound, they may attempt one additional action if they pass Stamina. It must occur at their next available DEX rank; delaying it requires another Stamina roll for each round, and any failure means death before the action. After acting, they die.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Dying Blows (Option) (brp-orc#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one final action after a successful Stamina roll, followed by death; a world can remove the option or broaden eligible actions to set how dramatic a fatal injury can be.

rules.statement: Armor’s value is subtracted from damage that gets through, and damage at or below zero causes no injury. When a shield and armor both apply, subtract both values; under the random-value option, roll armor separately for each damaging attack.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Armor; Random Armor Values (Option) (brp-orc#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fixed damage reduction, with an optional per-hit random value; a world can choose fixed or variable protection to set how reliable armor is.

rules.statement: A character normally regains 1D3 hit points each week. First Aid success immediately restores 1D3 per wound; under poor care a Difficult First Aid or Medicine success is required for weekly healing, failure prevents healing, and a fumble causes 1D3 extra damage.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Healing Naturally; Conditions of Medical Care (brp-orc#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weekly recovery of 1D3 hit points; a world can alter recovery according to care and exertion, making inadequate treatment risky.

rules.statement: Healing restores 1D6 hit points per spell level used in the example: Healing 1 restores 3 points, while Healing 2 restores 4. Each level used costs 3 power points, and healing can return an unconscious character to consciousness when the gamemaster judges their condition allows it.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 159–160, combat example (brp-orc#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restoring a random 1D6 hit points per level for 3 power points per level; a world can change the recovery or price, with the caster’s reserve limiting repeated use.

rules.statement: An aura attack makes visible targets resist with POW against the attacker’s aura total, calculated as the average of SIZ, POW, and CHA rounded up. A target that fails is unable to initiate actions until the round ends; a fumble instead demoralizes them for the rest of that round, making actions Difficult and potentially prompting surrender or flight.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 163, Aura Attacks (brp-orc#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a brief, round-long restriction on self-directed action after failed resistance; a setting can intensify or soften the response, with the target’s resistance and the attack’s visible, social nature setting its limits.

rules.statement: Acid deals damage each round: weak acid causes 1D3−1, strong acid 1D4, and very strong acid 1D6+1. Armor halves damage, rounded up, for 1D3 rounds; very strong acid also destroys armor after 1D6 rounds of exposure.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 161, Acid (brp-orc#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ongoing damage and temporary armor mitigation; a world can vary armor coverage or acid strength, with prolonged exposure consuming armor and harming the victim.

rules.statement: A character exposed to environmental asphyxiation can initially hold their breath with a CON×10 roll, then faces progressively lower CON multipliers each round, starting at CON×5 in the second round. Once a roll fails, the character takes damage each subsequent round until escape, unconsciousness, or death; deliberate choking instead calls for CON×1 each round or causes 1D6 damage.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Pages 167–168, Choking, Drowning, and Asphyxiation (brp-orc#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to worsening resistance followed by recurring damage; a world can change the starting grace period or damage by the hazard, with loss of breathable air driving the escalating cost.

rules.statement: After contracting a disease, a character makes a recovery check each morning beginning on day two, starting at CON×2 and increasing the multiplier by 1 each day; a fumble reduces it by 1. Rest and care are required, and each outstanding strenuous or adverse condition reduces the multiplier by 1; medical treatment can help but cannot replace a successful natural recovery check.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Disease, p. 170 (brp-orc#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to daily, progressively easier recovery while resting; a world can make diseases persist longer or recovery harder under strain, because illness requires time and care.

rules.statement: For diseases that cause characteristic loss, each failed recovery check increases illness severity: after 1, 2, 3, or 4+ failures, the loss is respectively 1 characteristic point per week, day, hour, or minute. The first point is lost within 24 hours of infection, and reaching 0 in a characteristic usually means death or permanent debilitation.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Illness Severity Table, p. 170 (brp-orc#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating losses after failed recovery checks; a world can change the failure thresholds or loss rate to reflect how dangerous its diseases are.

rules.statement: An explosion’s damage is set by its dice and radius, with a guideline of 2 meters of radius per D6; damage drops by 1D6 for every 2 meters from the center, reaching none beyond the radius. Demolition can increase damage and radius by up to 50%, or halve both to weaken the charge.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Explosions, p. 171 (brp-orc#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to damage diminishing with distance; a world can change blast size or falloff, with explosive strength and demolition skill determining the cost.

rules.statement: Fire damages exposed characters at the end of the round: a candle deals 1 point, a torch 1D6, a bonfire 1D6+2, a burning structure 2D6, and intense fire 3D6 per round. Intense fire also causes 1D6 extra damage each following turn; protection subtracts its value, while a fire can be extinguished in at least one round, with a failed Luck roll allowing it to continue.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Fire and Heat, p. 172 (brp-orc#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recurring exposure damage reduced by protection; a world can adjust intensity, duration, and ignition risk to reflect the hazard and available defenses.

rules.statement: A declared knockback compares final damage against the target’s SIZ; if the target loses the resistance contest, they move 1 meter for each 5 damage points exceeding their SIZ and must pass Agility to stay upright. A mounted target can add the mount’s SIZ after a successful Ride, Drive, or Pilot check.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Knockback, pp. 173–174 (brp-orc#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to knockback only when damage overcomes the target’s size; a world can lower the threshold to make powerful impacts more frequent, at the cost of greater displacement.

rules.statement: A declared knockout attempt is a Difficult targeted attack against a living being with a defined head; if damage after armor reaches the major-wound threshold, the target takes 1 damage and is unconscious for 1D10+10 rounds. A lesser wound instead deals the weapon’s minimum damage after armor without knocking the target out.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Knockout Attacks, p. 174 (brp-orc#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a nonlethal knockout only when a sufficiently severe hit lands; a world can broaden eligible targets or change unconsciousness duration, trading realism for cinematic control.

rules.statement: Poison POT is resisted against CON: if it overcomes CON, it deals its full POT as damage; otherwise it usually deals half POT, rounded up. Each dose is resisted separately, and damage begins after the poison’s delay—usually three combat rounds for fast poisons or three turns for slower ones; an antidote taken within six turns subtracts its POT from the poison’s POT.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Poisons and Poison Antidotes, p. 176 (brp-orc#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delayed, potency-based harm reduced by a timely antidote; a world can vary onset and antidote compatibility because different poisons act differently.

rules.statement: Radiation exposure is resisted with CON against radiation POT, with effects checked at a rate determined by intensity: every 30 days at POT 5, weekly at 10, daily at 15, hourly at 20, every minute at 25, and each combat round at 30+. Failed checks produce the listed escalating illness, damage, blindness, sterility, or death; at POT 25 death follows within CON/2 hours without suitable medical assistance, while at 30+ death follows in 1D3 combat rounds.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Radiation Effects Table, pp. 177–178 (brp-orc#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to worsening effects as radiation potency rises and checks become more frequent; a world can make radiation beneficial or alter its severity to suit its genre.

rules.statement: A magic item can cast spells it knows using its own power points, or its owner’s if the item uses the owner’s reserve. At 0 points it cannot be used; its user may transfer 1 point from their body into it each combat round to recharge it.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Powers, p. 188 (brp-orc#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an item with a finite, damage-limited reserve; a setting can allow owner-powered items or larger reserves, at the cost of the owner’s power points.

rules.statement: A magic item can store up to twice its maximum power points, but points above its normal maximum disappear in the same way as a character’s excess points. Damage reduces the item’s storage limit, and destroying it makes it mundane and permanently loses any POW invested in it.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Powers, p. 188 (brp-orc#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to capacity that falls as the item is damaged; a world can make items more durable or storage more generous, but must decide what happens to invested power if the item is destroyed.

rules.statement: A magic spell bound permanently to an item is always active at full strength and needs no power points, but creating such an item costs five times the usual POW cost.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Powers, p. 188 (brp-orc#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a continuously active effect with a fivefold creation cost; a world can restrict which spells may be made permanent or change that cost to limit persistent magic.

rules.statement: A mutated item is treated as alive and heals at its creator’s rate; anyone can use it after succeeding at a Stamina roll. If it is destroyed, its invested CON and mutations are lost.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Powers, pp. 188–189 (brp-orc#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a living item that requires a successful Stamina roll to use; a world can make access easier, but risks losing the invested traits if the item is destroyed.

rules.statement: A character with a psychic ability recognizes that an item has psychic abilities automatically, and can work out how to use it with an Idea roll. A character without psychic abilities has more difficulty identifying it.
