locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Psychic Abilities, p. 189 (brp-orc#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to psychic users detecting such items automatically and learning their use with a roll; a world can make detection harder or open to non-psychics, trading secrecy for broader access.

rules.statement: Underwater, non-impaling weapons deal half damage, and characters gain 3 extra armor points against those weapons. A swimmer must roll Swim each turn to get into position, combat actions are limited by Swim skill in most cases, and combat costs twice the usual fatigue.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Underwater Combat, p. 180 (brp-orc#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these underwater penalties for ordinary characters; a world can exempt acclimated aquatic beings, while retaining the environmental costs for others.

rules.statement: Without protection in vacuum, a character who does not first exhale takes 1D6+2 damage each combat round from lung collapse. Hemorrhage deals 1 damage in the first round, then 2, 4, 8, and so on each subsequent round; protective-suit armor may delay this by one round per armor point.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Vacuum, p. 180 (brp-orc#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating harm each round without protection; a world can reduce or delay it with suitable suits, making protection an equipment and availability question.

rules.statement: In zero gravity, a character attempting combat or physical activity rolls Agility each round; failure makes those actions Difficult. Unless braced, an impact can knock back both the character and attacker, while impact damage is halved, rounded up.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Zero-gravity Combat, p. 182 (brp-orc#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an Agility roll each round and extra knockback when unbraced; a world can let specialized gear remove the orientation and impact problems.

rules.statement: Creating an artifact costs its maker 1 permanent POW for each invested sorcery spell; its power-point capacity is the greater of the maker’s normal power points or the artifact’s SIZ. It can hold up to twice that capacity, but points above its normal capacity disappear as they do for a character.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Sorcery (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a finite, item-held reserve with costly creation; a world can make artifacts draw on users instead, shifting the burden to each user’s power points.

rules.statement: An artifact at 0 power points becomes inert or unconscious, and a user can recharge it by transferring 1 power point from their body per combat round. Damage reduces its storage limit; if it is broken or destroyed, it cannot regain artifact status, and destruction also loses invested POW.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Sorcery (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow bodily recharging and damage-sensitive capacity; a world can make recharging easier, at the cost of weakening the item’s scarcity and vulnerability.

rules.statement: A psychic item’s creator or the gamemaster chooses who may use it. A would-be user must either win a power-point-versus-power-point resistance contest or succeed at a Difficult Luck roll; the item has ordinary hit points, does not heal naturally, and stops working if destroyed.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Psychic items (preceding Equipment with Sorcery) (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to creator-set access and a contest or Difficult Luck check to overcome it; a world can make access unrestricted, removing the item’s built-in gate.

rules.statement: An artifact with a spell that remains active permanently costs twice the usual POW to create. Spells cast from an artifact otherwise follow their normal rules.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Sorcery (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to doubling creation cost for always-on effects; a world can lower that cost, making permanent enchantments more common.

rules.statement: A gadget’s superpowers remain invested permanently unless the gadget is destroyed. Its characteristics and skills should support the powers it uses; it automatically fails a resistance roll if it lacks the relevant characteristic.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Superpowers (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent powers on a destructible device, with its own capabilities determining use; a world can make powers temporary or user-dependent, reducing device autonomy.

rules.statement: When an item combines power types, all its powers use the same resource pool, and recharging must satisfy each power type’s rules. The item needs the characteristics or skills required by its powers, and when either of two values can be used for an action, use the higher where appropriate.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Multiple Power Types, p. 190 (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one shared resource pool and all required capabilities; a world can keep separate pools, increasing bookkeeping and limiting cross-use of reserves.

rules.statement: An item can require a minimum or maximum characteristic or a skill threshold to use. If someone tries to use it without meeting a requirement, the gamemaster may impose extra fatigue, make associated skill rolls Difficult, or require a characteristic roll to avoid mishaps.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Equipment with Requirements, p. 190 (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to enforceable thresholds with possible fatigue, difficulty, or mishap costs; a world can waive them, allowing broader access at the cost of less distinction between users.

rules.statement: Limited-use equipment is normally assumed to have adequate refills with enough time and planning. When supplies are hard to obtain, the gamemaster may require a Research, Status, or Luck roll; refilling resources are usually free or cost two or three Wealth levels less than the equipment.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Charges or Limited-Use Equipment, p. 190 (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to abstracting routine supplies, with acquisition rolls when circumstances make them scarce; a world can make ammunition or fuel consistently scarce, adding a recurring supply cost.

rules.statement: A weapon skill applies to weapons in its class. The gamemaster may let a character use a similar weapon from another class at a Difficult temporary rating; experience earned that way is checked against and added to the base chance, not the temporary rating.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Using Weapons of the Same Class / Using Weapons of Different Classes, pp. 197–198 (brp-orc#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to class-based skill transfer, halved when treated as Difficult; a world can disallow cross-class use, making specialized training more restrictive.

rules.statement: Primitive, ancient, and medieval armor provides half its normal protection against firearms; modern armor provides half protection against energy weapons, while advanced armor normally works at full value against all attacks. Apply the reduction after determining armor protection and round up; armor already listing separate protection values is not reduced again.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Armor and Firearms, p. 203 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to halving protection across the stated technology gaps; a setting can change which weapons count as advanced, reflecting how armor materials fare against newer attacks.

rules.statement: When a firearm’s attack roll reaches or exceeds its malfunction number, it cannot fire until cleared. A dud can be cycled or ejected in one round; clearing a jam takes 1D6 rounds and a successful firearm or Repair skill roll, whichever is higher, and a failed attempt can be repeated with another 1D6 rounds; a 96–00 repair roll destroys the weapon beyond casual repair.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Malfunctions, p. 203 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed malfunction threshold and repair delays; a world can make weapons more or less reliable, with unreliable designs costing time and possibly the weapon.

rules.statement: Reloading a handgun, rifle, or shotgun takes one combat round for every two rounds loaded, and exchanging a clip, energy cell, or battery takes one round; changing a machine-gun belt takes two rounds. Under time pressure, a character may load one round and fire a single shot at half their normal DEX rank, rounded up.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Reloading Firearms, p. 203 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these reload times; a world can speed up or slow down reloading to reflect equipment design and the value of exposing oneself while handling ammunition.

rules.statement: Aiming-area fire doubles a ranged weapon’s attacks per round but reduces the chance to hit to one-fifth of the shooter’s skill; resolve a hit as a normal success, and choose randomly among multiple targets if needed. A prepared shooter with a laser sight or equivalent and a weapon skill above 60% may avoid this reduction at the gamemaster’s discretion.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Unaimed Shots, p. 204 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trading accuracy for twice as many attacks; allow targeting aids and preparation to relax that cost when the setting supports them.

rules.statement: Energy armor can be set to any protection value from 1 to 20, taking 5 DEX ranks to adjust. It spends power charges each combat round equal to its set protection, plus one additional charge per damage point it absorbs; a standard supply holds 200 charges, and it cannot be worn with other armor.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Advanced Armor, p. 208 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to adjustable protection paid for from a finite charge reserve; a world can change the capacity or charge drain, balancing stronger defense against shorter operating time.

rules.statement: Layering soft, pliable armor adds its usual protection and encumbrance. When hard armor is layered with anything other than soft armor, add the protection values but triple the encumbrance of the less protective piece.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Layering Armor, p. 209 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to combining protection while penalizing mismatched hard layers with triple encumbrance; a world can loosen or tighten the burden to represent its armor technology.

rules.statement: Putting on armor takes one combat round per point of protection if the wearer is prepared and conditions are calm; removal allows 3 protection points per round, or 4 after a successful Agility roll. Difficult circumstances can increase donning time, and removing armor uses its maximum protection rating when armor values are random.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Putting Armor On / Taking Armor Off, p. 209 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow donning and faster removal; a world can alter these times to reflect armor complexity, with rushed or adverse conditions imposing additional delay.

rules.statement: A slung shield adds half its protection value, rounded up, to protection at a hit location it covers when that location is struck; bucklers, primitive shields, and energy shields cannot be slung. A thrown shield is an improvised attack with 10-meter range and a 5% base chance to hit.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Slung Shields, p. 210 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to partial protection from a shield carried passively and the stated restriction on which shields can be slung; a world can vary coverage, trading active defense for protection while carried.

rules.statement: Artillery normally attacks an area of SIZ 40, about four meters in radius; a smaller target incurs a 1% hit-chance penalty for each SIZ point below 40. Guided missiles make the operator’s skill use Easy, while a self-guided missile hits automatically except on 99 or 00; a target’s dodge is Difficult, and electronic jamming makes the missile attack Difficult.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Artillery Weapon Effects / Guided Missiles, p. 212 (brp-orc#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to area targeting and guided accuracy with difficult evasion; a setting can make guidance or jamming more or less effective, changing the cost of relying on electronic systems.

rules.statement: For explosions that inflict damage over a radius, damage decreases by 1D6 for each meter beyond the initial radius; in the advanced explosive notes, the reduction is 1D per range increment. Non-damaging effects such as illumination or smoke instead fill or affect the stated area.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Modern Explosives, p. 216; Advanced Explosives, p. 217 (brp-orc#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reducing blast damage by one die at each distance step; a setting can change the decrement or radius to reflect its explosives and desired lethality.

rules.statement: A struck target hit by a flame-producing weapon must fail a Luck roll to catch fire, then takes 1D6 damage immediately and each following round until the fire is put out or neutralized. Plasma weapons require a Difficult Luck roll for this effect.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Modern Explosives, p. 216; Advanced Explosives, p. 217 (brp-orc#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ongoing 1D6 fire damage after a failed Luck check; a world can make ignition more or less likely to set the danger of incendiary weapons.

rules.statement: A medi-kit makes First Aid attempts Easy and doubles the hit points restored by a successful attempt. An auto-doc has 100% Medicine and First Aid skill; a successful treatment restores double the hit points and halves recovery time.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Medical Equipment, p. 223 (brp-orc#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these fixed treatment bonuses; a setting can make advanced medical devices rarer or more costly to limit access.

rules.statement: When damage exceeds an inanimate object’s armor value, subtract the armor from the damage, then reduce both its hit points and armor value by the remaining damage. At zero hit points, a smaller-than-human object is destroyed; a larger object has a human-sized hole in the damaged section.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Damage to Inanimate Objects, p. 224 (brp-orc#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to armor and hit points degrading together under penetrating damage; a world can make structures tougher or allow repeated attacks to weaken them faster.

rules.statement: Natural armor values of substances do not decline from repeated attacks. A gamemaster may instead rule that successful attacks aimed at the same spot reduce armor by 1 each time, until a later attack breaks through.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Armor Value of Substances, p. 224–225 (brp-orc#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to durable natural armor; a world can allow focused attacks to wear down a specific spot to model cracking or deliberate breaching.

rules.statement: Most powers consume power points; when a character has none left, they become unconscious.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Teaching the Rules, p. 232 (brp-orc#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to power-point fuel and unconsciousness at zero; a world can change the reserve or consequence because powers exhaust their users.

rules.statement: A character with 0 hit points dies.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Teaching the Rules, p. 232 (brp-orc#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to death at zero hit points; a world can soften or replace this threshold to make injury less final.

rules.statement: The optional Fate Points rule lets players spend power points to change dice results and introduce narrative elements.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Optional Rule Checklist—Miscellaneous, p. 230 (brp-orc#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spending power points for a result adjustment or narrative addition; a world can limit such interventions because they draw on the same resource as powers.

rules.statement: A personality trait is rated from 0 to 100; its paired opposite has the complementary value, so a rating of 90 corresponds to 10 in the opposite trait. A trait can be rolled against: success means the character follows that trait, while failure means they follow its opposite.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Personality Traits, pp. 240–241 (brp-orc#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to complementary paired ratings and a roll to resolve behavior; a world can make traits more or less influential, with character agency as the main limit.

rules.statement: For a nonplayer character’s trait, the gamemaster may use the rating directly as the success threshold: for example, Aggressive 90 means a roll of 01–90 produces an aggressive response and 91–100 a passive one. Traits may instead guide roleplaying without a roll.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Personality Traits, p. 241 (brp-orc#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rolling only when the response is uncertain; a world can make reactions automatic or routinely rolled, trading speed for unpredictability.

rules.statement: A successful Psychology treatment can shift one paired personality trait by the amount of SAN that the same result would restore. Use the same treatment time as for SAN restoration.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Skills and Personality Traits, p. 241 (brp-orc#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing gradual change through Psychology at the SAN-restoration rate; a world can restrict or expand the permitted shift, with treatment time as its cost.

rules.statement: For a player character, traits can augment activities or be consulted when provoked, and successful use can earn an experience check. If the player succeeds on one trait but chooses to act according to its opposite, they automatically receive an experience check for that opposite trait; increasing one trait reduces its opposite.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Personality Traits and Player Characters, p. 241 (brp-orc#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to player control with trait-based checks and paired adjustments; a world can make traits more binding, at the cost of limiting choice.

rules.statement: Successful rolls made by a player character whose player is absent do not award experience points, whether the character is run by the gamemaster or another player.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Absent Player Characters (brp-orc#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to withholding experience for absent players’ characters; a world can award it anyway, trading attendance-based fairness for uninterrupted progression.

rules.statement: During a break, the game world can be treated as having no time pass, or the break can represent an in-world time jump. If that jump is substantial, the group may resolve healing, experience checks, and training.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Take a Break if You Need It (brp-orc#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pausing world time unless the gamemaster declares a jump; a world can make breaks advance time, potentially triggering recovery and training.

rules.statement: A character is allied with an allegiance only when its score is at least 20 points higher than every other score and the character consciously acknowledges it. Allegiance scores never fall below 0, and reaching 100 or more does not by itself make the character an ally or an apotheosis.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Allegiance; Creating Allegiances (pp. 250–252) (brp-orc#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring both the 20-point lead and acknowledgment; a setting can change the threshold or omit allegiance benefits to reflect how demanding its beliefs are.

rules.statement: After an adventure, a character whose conduct favored an allegiance may test it; success adds 1D6 points. When an allied character acts against that allegiance, the gamemaster may test it: a roll above the score adds 1D4–1D8 points to an opposed allegiance, according to the severity, while a roll equal to or below it has no consequence.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Increasing Allegiance; Maintaining Allegiance (pp. 251–252) (brp-orc#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to awarding points for favored conduct and risking opposed-allegiance gains for violations; a world can make tests more or less frequent to set the pressure of religious or ideological commitment.

rules.statement: A successful allegiance test can grant a reserve of power points equal to up to 10% of the current allegiance score, usable only as the character spends their last normal power points and at most three times per session. Alternatively, once per session a successful test can grant temporary hit points up to 20% of the score, or a pool equal to the whole score that can be assigned to skill rolls before rolling, up to three times per session; unused temporary hit points vanish at session end, and none of these benefits reduce the allegiance score.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Benefits to Allegiance (p. 252) (brp-orc#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing these benefits only after a successful allegiance test; a setting can change the options or limits to decide how concretely devotion sustains its adherents.

rules.statement: An allied character can seek intervention from their power by rolling against the chance of a critical success; on a critical result, the power aids them directly, through an agent, or through a miraculous natural event. A character can attempt an allegiance test after using this benefit.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Benefits to Allegiance (p. 252) (brp-orc#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a rare, potentially extraordinary intervention on a critical result; a world can make aid more reliable or restrained to reflect the power’s reach and willingness to act.

rules.statement: At 100 or more points in an allegiance, an allied character may be offered apotheosis, but it requires acceptance and demonstrated worth. The resulting living avatar keeps free will, may still betray the force, and can receive tailored benefits such as limited immunity to aging and disease, increased hit points, doubled ratings in three suitable skills, a powerful artifact, or doubled maximum power points; communication with the force is then possible at POW×3 and may become intrusive.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Apotheosis (pp. 252–253) (brp-orc#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making apotheosis an optional offer at 100+ points rather than an automatic change; a world can vary its rewards and intrusiveness to show what service to a force demands.

rules.statement: A passion roll can inspire one skill for one task or situation, for no more than a day, and only once per scene; its benefit cannot combine with another skill augment. Critical, special, and ordinary success add 50%, 30%, and 20% respectively, while failure imposes −10% on further rolls in the scene; a fumble reduces the passion by 1D10% and causes despair, during which the character can generally only flee or hide. Despair lasts 1D10 rounds on 1–3, 1D10+10 rounds on 4–7, until sunset or a similar interval on 8–9, and 1D3 days on 10.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Using Passions: Inspiration; Despair (p. 255) (brp-orc#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one inspiration attempt per scene, with risky failure outcomes; a world can adjust duration and penalties to determine how forcefully emotion drives behavior.

rules.statement: A passion rated at 80% or higher may prompt a mandatory roll when conduct conflicts with it; the gamemaster may reduce it below 80% or pit it against another passion, letting the winning passion guide the character’s choice. A passion reduced to 0% is removed and cannot normally be regained.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Mandatory Rolls; Gaining a Passion (pp. 255–256) (brp-orc#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating ratings of 80% or higher as potentially compelling; a world can change that threshold or permit recovery to tune how binding strong feelings are.

rules.statement: Reputation can identify a character or augment a suitable Communication skill. When used to augment, a critical, special, or ordinary success grants +50%, +30%, or +20%; failure gives −20%, and a fumble gives −50%. Recognition is rolled against the subject’s Reputation, and people farther away socially or geographically may apply modifiers.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Using Reputation; Reputation Modifiers (pp. 258–259) (brp-orc#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to public deeds building durable reputation and to audience distance modifying recognition; a world can adjust the reach of news to determine how widely fame travels.

rules.statement: Starting Sanity (SAN) is POW×5; the temporary-insanity threshold (TIS) is half starting SAN and remains fixed even when current SAN changes. A setting may instead set TIS equal to POW.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Sanity Mechanics (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to half starting SAN as the crisis threshold; a setting may use POW for a lower threshold and more frequent breakdowns.

rules.statement: When a Sanity roll fails, the character loses the amount determined by the gamemaster; some especially horrific events also cause a reduced loss on a successful roll. Losing SAN equal to or above TIS within five minutes causes temporary insanity, with a 1D6 result determining its form and 1D8 its duration.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Sanity Mechanics; Temporary Insanity; Temporary Insanity Duration (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed SAN checks and fixed five-minute accumulation window; a setting can adjust losses and thresholds to make psychological crises more or less common.

rules.statement: At SAN 0, a character is permanently insane and leaves player control; recovery requires divine intervention or another major process, if the gamemaster permits it. Restored SAN cannot exceed the character’s starting maximum, which can be reduced to 100 minus a relevant skill rating.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Sanity Mechanics; Maximum Sanity (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to removal from play at zero SAN; a setting can allow major recovery, at the cost of extensive treatment or intervention.

rules.statement: SAN may be restored by defeating a source of SAN loss for up to half its threatened loss, successful psychotherapy for 1D3−1 points, or reaching 91% in a skill for a one-time 2D6 points. The gamemaster may also allow drugs or powers, and all recovery remains subject to the character’s maximum SAN.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Restoring Sanity Points (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed recovery methods and cap; a setting can broaden or restrict recovery according to available treatment and powers.

rules.statement: Repeated exposure to the same SAN-loss source may have reduced effects or require no new roll if the character has become familiar with it. Successful and failed SAN rolls can cause different losses, including losses on success for some sources.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Sanity Costs by Situation; Sanity Losses (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed situation losses and allow desensitization; a setting can keep repeated exposure dangerous or reduce it as characters adapt.

rules.statement: A creature lacking a characteristic cannot be affected by attacks or conditions that target that characteristic. For example, creatures without CON ignore CON-resisted poison and disease, while those without INT ignore effects on rational thought but may still be affected through emotion.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Creatures Without Characteristics (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immunity when a creature has no relevant characteristic; a setting can decide which effects target emotion or other attributes instead.

rules.statement: An insect swarm stings each attacked character every combat round until the swarm is escaped, deterred, or destroyed, and gives up after 2D6 rounds. After 1D6 hours, victims resist venom based on CON against potency calculated from the sting count; covering, protective gear, or antivenom can reduce or prevent the threat.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Natural Animals; Insect Swarm (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to repeated stings followed by delayed venom; a setting can change swarm size, venom severity, or protection to tune the hazard.

rules.statement: In ghostly combat, the ghost and target make a POW-versus-POW resistance roll; the loser usually loses 1D3 power points. The contest repeats each round until someone is unconscious or flees, and a ghost that reduces a target to zero power points may possess them but remains tied to its haunting site.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Ghost (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to power-point attrition and site-bound possession; a setting can vary the ghost’s drain or possession behavior to reflect its nature.

rules.statement: A ghoul gains 1 power point per 3 SIZ points of corpse consumed, spends 1 each morning to remain animated, and spends another 1 for each hour in sunlight. Its howl costs 1 power point and can stun targets that fail a power-points-versus-INT resistance roll.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Ghoul (brp-orc#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to corpse-fed upkeep and a paid stunning howl; a setting can change the sustenance rate or sunlight burden to alter the ghoul’s survival pressure.

rules.statement: A mummy is twice as easy to ignite as a normal target. Once burning, it takes normal fire damage, but the chance that the fire goes out is halved; fire-based powers follow the same rule.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Mummy, p. 273 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to increased ignition and reduced chance of extinguishing; a setting can tune or omit this vulnerability to reflect how its undead bodies work.

rules.statement: A skeleton has hit points equal to its SIZ and no CON. It ignores bleeding and impaling special effects, and thrusting weapons deal no damage unless the hit is special or critical; even then, secondary effects are ignored. Any damaging blow also has a destruction chance of damage dealt ×4 percent, which instantly shatters it if successful.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Skeleton, p. 274 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed immunities and damage-scaled shattering chance; a world can adjust the exceptions or multiplier to suit how brittle its animated bones are.

rules.statement: A troll heals 1D3 hit points each combat round, or 1 hit point per wounded location if hit locations are used. Sunlight and fire damage do not regenerate; regeneration also stops once it is dead.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Troll, p. 274 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rapid round-by-round healing except against fire, sunlight, and death; a world can change the healing rate or its counters to define troll physiology.

rules.statement: A unicorn can restore hit points by touching a wound with its horn, spending 1 power point per hit point healed. It can reattach a severed limb for at least 6 power points; curing each point of attribute loss from poison or disease costs 1 permanent POW, and it can detect poison by touch.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Unicorn, p. 275 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to healing paid from power points, with permanent POW lost for curing attribute damage; a world can change these prices to make unicorn aid more or less scarce.

rules.statement: A vampire that bites and damages a target may, while remaining attached, drain 1D6 STR or power points each later round. If the target has no STR left, it may drain CON instead; reaching 0 CON kills the victim. Drained STR, CON, or power points transfer to the vampire as power points, capped at its CON, and excess is lost.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Vampire—Powers: Blood Drain, p. 276 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a continuing grapple-based drain that converts the victim’s loss into the vampire’s power, capped by CON; a world can change the rate or cap to set the danger and feeding cost.

rules.statement: An angel’s holy fire covers a three-meter-square area, costs 10 power points, and can be used once per day. Aligned pious characters may avoid damage with a successful allegiance roll; others take 10D6 damage, and the flames end at the end of the round.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Angel—Powers: Holy Fire, p. 279 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a short-lived area attack with a substantial power cost and one-use-per-day limit; a world can adjust its range, price, or alignment protection as expressions of divine authority.

rules.statement: A greater demon’s blight automatically affects an area within POW ×100 meters. It takes 30 days minus the demon’s POW to become manifest, and recovery takes a number of months equal to its POW; the demon cannot hide or suppress the effect.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Demon, Greater—Powers: Blight, p. 280 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an unavoidable, slow environmental corruption with a longer recovery period; a world can change the radius and durations to set the scale of demonic aftermath.

rules.statement: An elemental disappears when reduced to 0 hit points or when it spends its last power point. It does not heal lost hit points or regenerate power points, and normal weapons and firearms cannot harm it, though opposing elementals can.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Elementals, p. 281 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a being sustained by its remaining body and power, vulnerable mainly to suitable supernatural opposition; a world can broaden its vulnerabilities or add recovery to change how it can be opposed.

rules.statement: A werewolf can shift among human, hybrid, and wolf forms by spending 5 DEX ranks, with no power-point cost. It can move directly from any one form to another.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Werewolf—Powers: Transformation, p. 278 (brp-orc#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a form change paid in action capacity rather than power points; a world can change the DEX cost or make shifting voluntary or condition-triggered.

rules.statement: A creature with the stench feature can nauseate nearby breathers; a failed Stamina roll makes actions against it Difficult for 1D6+2 rounds. A creature with the disorienting-appearance feature imposes the same duration and difficulty on attackers who fail a POW-versus-POW resistance roll.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Chaotic Features table, pp. 285–286 (brp-orc#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed resistance test and 1D6+2-round penalty; a setting can change the trigger or duration to tune how strongly appearance and stench hinder combat.

rules.statement: A creature with the reflection feature sends 1D6+2 points of incoming magic or sorcery back at its user; determine the reflected amount randomly on each turn a spell is cast against it.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Chaotic Features table, p. 285 (brp-orc#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reflecting a random 1D6+2 points each casting; a world can alter the amount or eligible magic, with stronger reflection making spellcasting against the creature riskier.

rules.statement: A creature with acidic blood sprays corrosive acid when physically wounded. Those within one meter test Luck to avoid 1D3 damage; acid eats through armor round by round, and remains corrosive for 1D6+2 rounds unless neutralized sooner.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Alien, Xenomorph, p. 286 (brp-orc#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-meter spray, a Luck test, and 1D6+2 rounds of corrosion; a world can change spread or persistence, with armor and time limiting the hazard.

rules.statement: A blob takes only 1 point of damage from physical weapons, and fire and electrical attacks deal half damage, rounded up. It can engulf a target on a successful attack, then digest it starting the next round for 1D3−1 damage each round; escape requires a successful Difficult Effort roll, and protective gear must fully enclose the victim and lasts rounds equal to its armor value.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Blob, p. 286 (brp-orc#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated damage resistances, engulfment, and Difficult escape; a world can tune damage and gear duration, balancing the blob’s danger against escape opportunities.

rules.statement: A blob regenerates 1 hit point per combat round until it reaches full hit points.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Blob, p. 286 (brp-orc#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 1 hit point each round up to maximum; a world can raise, lower, or suppress recovery to set how quickly the creature can be worn down.

rules.statement: A xenomorph can make two claw attacks in a round and bite 5 DEX ranks later; if both claws hit, it tries to grapple and bite on the next round. When appropriate, it can substitute a tail lash for its bite.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Alien, Xenomorph, p. 286 (brp-orc#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the specified attack sequence and conditional follow-up; a world can change attack timing or substitutions to vary the creature’s combat pressure.

rules.statement: A giant robot’s adaptation to high pressure and vacuum is always active and costs no power points; it also has 100 extra hit points beyond its listed base hit points.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Robot, Giant, p. 287 (brp-orc#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to always-on environmental adaptation and the listed hit-point bonus; a world can require power expenditure or reduce the bonus, trading resilience for resource limits.

rules.statement: A cyborg’s mechanical components take an extra 1D6 damage from magnetic-based attacks.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Cyborg, p. 289 (brp-orc#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the additional 1D6 damage to components; a world can change the extra damage or the attacks that trigger it, making the drawback more or less costly.

rules.statement: For each listed creature body plan, roll a d20 and use its table to select the hit location; the listed fraction of the creature’s total hit points determines that location’s hit points. The tables differ by body plan, with results such as a snake’s tail, body, or head, and a winged humanoid’s limbs, torso, wings, or head.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Pages 301–302, creature hit location tables (brp-orc#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed d20 ranges and fractions; a world can change the body-plan tables to reflect anatomy, with location durability determined by the creature’s total hit points.

rules.statement: To find a location’s hit points, use the table matching the creature’s total hit points and the location’s fraction, rounding up as represented by the listed ranges. The passage also allows calculation from the stated fractions for greater precision.
locators: Basic Roleplaying ORC: Page 302, Creature Hit Location Table; page 303 (brp-orc#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the range table for quick allocation; a world can use the fractions directly for precision, at the cost of more calculation.
